title: Kalshi commits $1 million to support public housing residents in New York City
summary: Kalshi's four-year, $1 million commitment to the Public Housing Community Fund will help NYCHA residents train for careers in public health.
body_markdown:
Kalshi, the federally regulated prediction market, today announced a $1 million commitment to the Public Housing Community Fund (PHCF) to establish the Kalshi Public Housing Health Fund, expanding access to healthcare career opportunities for New York City Housing Authority (NYCHA) residents.


The four-year commitment will support the NYCHA Health Corps, a program designed to create pathways for public housing residents to pursue careers in healthcare while strengthening health services in their own communities.


The announcement was made at the Andrew Jackson Senior Center in the Bronx, alongside U.S. Congressman Ritchie Torres, PHCF Executive Director Alex Zablocki, NYCHA leadership, and community representatives.


"Kalshi is designed to empower people to predict, navigate, and manage the uncertainties of their world. And while I'm a passionate believer that markets can predict everything better, I don't believe they can solve every problem," said Tarek Mansour, CEO and Co-Founder of Kalshi. "New York City can be the financial capital of the world and be a place where we protect our most vulnerable. We see this as an investment in a safer, healthier, and more resilient future for New Yorkers."


Through the NYCHA Health Corps, public housing residents receive training, professional development, and hands-on experience working with public agencies and nonprofit organizations across New York City. Participants help connect fellow residents to critical health resources while building skills and experience for long-term careers in public health.


Kalshi's investment will support Health Corps participants through living allowances and career development opportunities, enabling residents to focus on their training and service to the community. In its second year, the program will welcome up to 35 public housing residents from across all five boroughs.


"NYCHA's residents are among our greatest strengths, and when we invest in them, we improve countless lives across public housing," said NYCHA Chief Executive Officer Lisa Bova-Hiatt. "We're thrilled that the NYCHA Health Corps will be reliably funded over the next four years, giving residents a lasting pathway into public health careers."


The program also strengthens healthcare outreach across New York City. Working with up to 20 host-site organizations, participants will provide structured, on-the-job health training and deliver health workforce training sessions and career development opportunities. The program's goal is to place 60 percent of graduates in health-related jobs or continued education within four months of completing service.


The partnership reflects Kalshi's broader commitment to investing in the communities where it operates. Founded and headquartered in New York City, Kalshi believes that building the next generation of financial markets goes hand in hand with supporting the communities around it.


Kalshi's $1 million commitment to the Public Housing Community Fund follows the company's


[$3 million partnership with Housing Works](https://news.kalshi.com/p/kalshi-housing-works-partnership)


, aimed at expanding access to quality healthcare, fueling workforce development, and strengthening community services for New Yorkers in need.
